comments.author: @BillFlavell
comments.text:
We have come to expect Tesla to be out front when it comes to developing novel technologies quickly, so seeing these Chinese robots now, rather than in 5 year's time is is genuinely stunning.

I notice though, that Unitree is following Boston Dynamics by focusing on gross motor skills such as locomotion, stability and agility whilst Tesla is putting effort into fine motor skills--manipulating small things with hands and fingers. Fine motor skills will be essential to build a robot capable of replacing almost every human worker.

Intelligence is also essential and I couldn't see any evidence that Unitree's robots have any intelligence. However, China has quite strong AI competency, so I imagine we won't have to wait long to see intelligence grafted onto these Chinese robots.

The rewards for combining all these elements and being able to manufacture these beasties efficiently and cheaply will surely be the biggest revolution in human history.
